AXP.rationale: American Express demonstrates strong fundamental health with consistent revenue and EPS growth trajectory (Q1 2026 revenue +9.3% YoY, EPS +17.6% YoY), high profitability (ROE 33%, net margin 26.6%), and a durable closed-loop business model with premium customer base. The company beat Q1 2026 expectations and reaffirmed 2026 guidance of 9-10% revenue growth and EPS of $17.30-$17.90. Valuation is attractive vs its own history: current P/E of 19.5x sits at the low end of its 19.2-25.3x 365-day range, and P/B of 6.4x is near the bottom of its 6.2-8.2x range. The stock has pulled back ~10% over the past quarter despite solid fundamentals, creating a modestly attractive entry. However, macro headwinds (rising 10Y yields at 4.41%, oil at $98/bbl, elevated VIX) and competitive pressures in premium cards temper enthusiasm. The Q1 earnings beat and reaffirmed guidance provide a near-term positive catalyst, though the stock's post-earnings dip suggests the market is already discounting some of this strength.
